Follow THISDAYLIVE on Google Add us as a preferred source to see more of our stories in Google Follow us on Google The Confederation of African Football (CAF) yesterday unveiled the five finalists for the prestigious CAF Men’s Player of the Year 2026 award, with reigning holder Achraf Hakimi, former winner Sadio Mané, Brahim Diaz, Ismael Saibari and Pape Gueye shortlisted for African football’s highest individual honour.
The final shortlist brings together three players from Morocco (Hakimi, Diaz, Saibari) and two from Senegal (Mane, Gueye) reflecting the outstanding performances of both nations during a remarkable year for African football, highlighted by Senegal’s triumph at the TotalEnergies CAF Africa Cup of Nations (AFCON) Morocco 2025 and Morocco’s run to the quarter-finals of the FIFA World Cup 2026.
The winner will be announced at the CAF Awards 2026, which will take place at the Professor Wole Soyinka Centre for Culture and the Arts (National Theatre) in Lagos, Nigeria, on Wednesday, 2 December 2026, starting at 19h00 local time (18h00 GMT).
The five finalists were selected from an initial list of 10 nominees following their exceptional contributions for club and country during the period under consideration.
The winner will be revealed during the CAF Awards 2026 ceremony in Lagos, which returns to Nigeria’s commercial capital for the first time since the 2014 edition.
